blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by having a draft model propose multiple tokens for the target model to verify in one pass. The speedup is governed by the expected acceptance length (EAL), yet standard training objectives such as cross-entropy, KL divergence, and total variation focus only on distribution matching or single-step overlap. Recent studies instead propose block-level training objectives, aiming to optimize EAL directly. However, these objectives remain surrogates rather than exact formulations of EAL. For example, some average later acceptance over target-distributed continuations rather than the verification branches selected by accepted tokens, introducing a covariance gap that can reverse the gradient direction. We analyze this gap and derive REAL, a real EAL training loss that uses path weights for unbiased estimation and Rao-Blackwellization for variance reduction. In a controlled loss-level comparison with a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B target and a Domino drafter, REAL outperforms WTV, VSD, DBLast, and the static LK baseline on probabilistic serving acceptance length across 9 task subsets and 5 evaluation seeds. These gains require only a change to the training loss, with no modification to the drafter architecture or inference procedure, demonstrating the practicality of real EAL training. A reference implementation of the REAL loss is available at https://github.com/King-ty/speculators/tree/real-loss.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by letting a small draft model propose multiple tokens that the target model verifies in one forward pass Leviathan et al. (2023) ; Chen et al. (2023) .
At a fixed draft and verification configuration, its speedup is governed by the expected number of accepted draft tokens per round, known as the expected acceptance length (EAL).
However, the dominant training objectives, such as cross-entropy and KL divergence, optimize token-level distribution matching rather than EAL Zhou et al. (2024) , causing a gap between the training objective and the inference metric.

在固定的草稿和验证配置中,其速度由每轮被接受的草稿的预期数来决定,称为预期接受长度(EAL).

blocks.en:
Acceptance-oriented objectives narrow this gap at different levels.
Single-step total variation losses optimize the one-step acceptance rate Goel et al. (2024) ; Samarin et al. (2026) , while recent work extends this idea to block-level objectives that aim to optimize EAL directly Zou et al. (2026) ; Karimi et al. (2026) ; Li et al. (2026b) ; Liu et al. (2026) ; Xia et al. (2026) .
For example, the end-to-end TV loss Li et al. (2026b) and the windowed total variation (WTV) objective of Xia et al. (2026) multiply per-step average acceptance rates over the proposal window.
However, this product form is a biased surrogate because an accepted token both extends the accepted prefix and determines the prefix used to verify the next draft token.
Multiplying marginal acceptance rates discards information about which tokens survive verification, so later acceptance is averaged over target-sampled paths rather than weighted by the propose-and-accept mass of the surviving branches, as shown in Figure 1 .
This mismatch appears as Cov ⁡ ( b k , a k + 1 ) \operatorname{Cov}(b_{k},a_{k+1}) , where b k b_{k} is the path weight under target sampling and a k + 1 a_{k+1} is the next-step acceptance rate.
The covariance can have either sign and can reverse the gradient direction, causing the surrogate to point away from the true objective, as shown in Section 3.1 .
In practice, we find this covariance positive throughout training, consistent with the observed gap between the branch estimate and the surrogate (Section 4.3 ).

blocks.en:
To address this gap, we derive an unbiased path estimator of the exact EAL for chain speculative decoding with stochastic rejection sampling.
On trajectories sampled from the target, each sampled token is reweighted by a path weight b i = min ⁡ ( 1 , q ⁡ ( y i ) / p ⁡ ( y i ) ) b_{i}=\min(1,q(y_{i})/p(y_{i})) to recover the true propose-and-accept branch distribution.
We then obtain the branch estimator by marginalizing the final token in each term via Rao–Blackwellization, reducing per-term variance while preserving the expected gradient Rao (1945) ; Blackwell (1947) .
The branch estimator is differentiable with respect to the draft parameters, allowing direct backpropagation during training.
Finally, we derive our final training loss, REAL , by adding an auxiliary CE term to stabilize training from scratch.

blocks.en:
We extensively evaluate REAL using a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE target Qwen Team (2026) , a Domino drafter Huang et al. (2026) , target-sampled data shared across methods, and a three-epoch training budget. REAL reaches 4.792 probabilistic acceptance length, outperforming all compared baselines (4.657–4.749) across 9 task subsets and 5 evaluation seeds, demonstrating the effectiveness of real EAL estimation.
The variant without Rao–Blackwellization achieves comparable acceptance length at serving temperature T = 1 T=1 , while REAL reduces aggregate gradient variance by 52–58% and generalizes better across serving temperatures.
Pure CE and REAL w/o CE also underperform REAL , showing that the real EAL term and the auxiliary CE term each contribute to the final result.
These gains require only a change to the training loss, with no modification to the drafter architecture or inference procedure, and improve average acceptance length across tasks and seeds, underscoring the practical significance of our method.

The conditional marginalization in the branch estimator is an instance of Rao–Blackwellization.
For each prefix contribution k k , the marginalized gradient is the conditional expectation of its trajectory-based counterpart given h k h_{k} , and therefore has no greater covariance.
Summing the mean-squared errors of the prefix-gradient estimators gives the ordering V Branch ≤ V Path V_{\textsc{Branch}}\leq V_{\textsc{Path}} , where V V denotes the sum of gradient mean-squared errors across prefix contributions.
The reduction in this summed mean-squared error equals the gradient variance removed by marginalizing the final token of each prefix term.
Thus, the branch estimator preserves the exact expected gradient while eliminating this source of sampling noise from each prefix contribution.
A detailed proof is given in Appendix B , and the sampling variance reduction is measured at the main scale in Section 4.4 .

blocks.en:
We use the Speculators framework Red Hat (2025) for training, with the frozen Qwen3.6-35B-A3B target model Qwen Team (2026) and the Domino drafter Huang et al. (2026) in mostly the same setting as the original Domino paper, changing only the loss and the draft block size to 8 (1 anchor and γ = 7 \gamma=7 ).
We select this target because its mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture and hybrid Gated Delta Network (GDN) structure reflect architectural choices in modern LLMs, with the aim of making our findings more transferable to current mainstream model architectures.
We select Domino as the drafter because it slightly outperformed other baselines in our preliminary comparisons.

Table 1 presents our main results, with overall and per-subset probabilistic acceptance length across 9 task subsets. REAL and its variant without RB top the table under probabilistic serving, reaching 4.792 and 4.791, respectively, ahead of all other compared methods (4.657–4.749).

blocks.en: 4.4 Ablations

blocks.en: We ablate four aspects: Rao–Blackwellization, the auxiliary CE term, serving temperature, and the training budget.

blocks.en:
REAL w/o RB ablates Rao–Blackwellization, keeping the sampled b k b_{k} in place of the marginalized a k a_{k} .
As shown in Table 3 , the per-term gradient variance is lower at every position in every checkpoint, with reductions of 76–84% at k = 2 k=2 and 52–58% for the aggregate gradient.
Rao–Blackwellization preserves the expected gradient while guaranteeing no greater covariance than the path estimator for each prefix-gradient contribution (Section 3.3 ).
As shown in Tables 1 and 11 , REAL w/o RB reaches 4.791 probabilistic AL, comparable to REAL (4.792), while its greedy AL (4.515) trails REAL (4.537).
Despite their similar final probabilistic AL at T = 1 T=1 , REAL performs better early in training (Figure 4 ) and generalizes better across serving temperatures (Table 5 ).
The pilot study further illustrates the optimization difficulties of sampled-path estimation (Appendix K ).

blocks.en:
To isolate whether the serving gains come from the EAL term or merely from the auxiliary CE term, we train pure CE without the EAL term, as well as REAL w/o CE and REAL w/o CE&RB.
Both variants without CE train to completion but stay below their CE-augmented counterparts in greedy and probabilistic serving AL (Table 4 ), as well as in the training EAL proxy trajectory (Figure 7 ), showing that the auxiliary CE term stabilizes training and improves serving performance with and without RB.
Although pure CE outperforms REAL on the training EAL proxy (Figure 7 ), its greedy and probabilistic serving AL are again below both REAL and REAL w/o RB (Table 4 ), demonstrating the effectiveness of the EAL loss term.
Thus, both the EAL term and the auxiliary CE term contribute to the final performance.

两种变体没有CE列车完成,但保持在其CE强化对等器下方的贪婪和概率服务AL(表4),以及训练EAL代理轨迹(图7),表明辅助CE术语稳定了培训,并改进了与RB一起和没有RB的服务性能.
虽然纯CE在培训EAL代理(图7)上表现优于REAL,但其贪婪和概率服务AL再次低于REAL和REAL w/o RB(表4),证明了EAL损失术语的有效性.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We have presented REAL , a real EAL training loss based on an unbiased and differentiable branch estimator for stochastic rejection sampling, using path weights to restore the propose-and-accept branch structure and Rao–Blackwellization to reduce per-term variance.
Our covariance analysis explains why products of marginal acceptance rates can reverse the optimization direction.
With only a change to training loss and no additional overhead, REAL achieves the best probabilistic acceptance length among the main compared objectives across 9 task subsets and 5 seeds at T = 1 T=1 , demonstrating its effectiveness.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了真实的EAL训练损失,这是基于一个无偏见且可区分的树枝采样模型,利用路径权重来恢复提议和接受树枝结构以及Rao-Blackwellization来减少每时每刻的差异。
我们的共性分析解释了为什么边际接受率的产品可以扭转优化方向.
由于只改变培训损失和不增加间接费用,REAL在9个任务子集和5个种子的比较目标中实现了最佳概率接受长度,T=1 T=1,表明其有效性。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
The evaluation is limited to one target model, one drafter architecture, and one sampled data recipe to enable controlled comparisons; broader evaluation across these settings is left for future work.
The VSD and DBLast comparisons use loss-level adaptations rather than full system reproductions, isolating the effect of the loss itself.
Our objective primarily targets probabilistic serving, and REAL is near-optimal under greedy serving.
blocks.zh:
评价限于一个目标模型、一个起草者架构和一个抽样数据配方,以便能够进行有控制的比较;这些背景下更广泛的评价留给今后工作。
VSD和DBLast的比较使用损失级的适应,而不是完整的系统复制,隔离损失本身的效果.
我们的目标主要针对概率服务,而REAL在贪婪服务下几乎是最佳的.

blocks.en:
The following findings shaped the main study. 1. The exact objective does not significantly outperform the surrogate in this setting. In this small-scale experiment, per-pair correlations are small, evaluation variance is large, and training is limited, so the comparison between training with J ^ Branch \widehat{J}_{\textsc{Branch}} and WTV remains inconclusive.
This provides a complementary setting in which exact estimation does not yield a clear serving advantage. 2. The path objective without CE is fragile. It collapsed in all four training runs through a positive feedback loop in which b → 0 b\to 0 concentrates the loss on surviving positions, and the path estimator has higher gradient variance than both WTV and the branch estimator.
Training with J ^ Branch \widehat{J}_{\textsc{Branch}} outperforms training with J ^ Path \widehat{J}_{\textsc{Path}} by 3.03 AL on average, a large and statistically significant advantage. 3. Detaching W W fails. The detached variant scores 1.56, supporting the role of the prefix-weight gradient in Equation ( 18 ) in stabilizing training. 4. The auxiliary loss stabilizes training. Across four independent training runs, training with J ^ Branch \widehat{J}_{\textsc{Branch}} without KL succeeds only once, reaching 3.53 serving AL in Table 15 .
Using J ^ Branch \widehat{J}_{\textsc{Branch}} with KL stabilizes training and reaches 3.63 serving AL, but does not significantly outperform training with either J ^ Branch \widehat{J}_{\textsc{Branch}} without KL or WTV.
This motivates the auxiliary CE term of the main study. 5. The data recipe matters. WTV scores 2.50 when trained on greedy decodes and 3.94 when trained on sampled continuations, supporting the requirement that real acceptance objectives train on target-sampled trajectories.
